rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, there is no evidence to favor any RNA/image encoder, profile setting, aggregation, or fusion strategy. The most informative first experiment is the simplest baseline: RNA-only, single profile, PCA n2000. It establishes a reference validation accuracy/F1 and provides a fixed anchor for later isolating the effects of multiprofile/aggregation, RNA representation, and image/multimodal fusion. Under a limited budget, this low-complexity, low-confounding baseline reduces uncertainty more efficiently than starting with a complex multimodal or multiprofile configuration.

The only completed experiment is a moderate RNA-only PCA single-profile baseline, so there is no evidence yet about whether the image modality contributes useful signal. config_010 tests an image-only ResNet50 single-profile baseline, isolating the effect of the image representation without confounding aggregation or fusion. This is the best next experiment because it directly clarifies whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing: if image-only performance is competitive, multimodal settings become more promising; if it is weak, the search should prioritize RNA profile/aggregation improvements instead.

RNA-only PCA singleprofile is much stronger than image-only ResNet singleprofile, so RNA is informative while image alone is weak. The key uncertainty is whether image features are complementary and whether simple fusion can improve over the RNA-only baseline. config_016 uses the same RNA and image encoders/profiles as the completed baselines and adds concat fusion, isolating the fusion effect without changing representation, profile, or aggregation. It is the best next use of budget because it directly tests the central multimodal question; a gain justifies further multimodal fusion/aggregation experiments, while a null or negative result redirects effort to RNA-only improvements.

config_016 is currently the best result (acc 0.527, F1 0.510), improving over RNA-only PCA (0.485) and image-only ResNet (0.208), suggesting the multimodal concat setup is promising but the fusion choice is not yet isolated. config_017 tests weighted fusion with the same single-profile PCA + ResNet representation, directly clarifying whether concat or weighted fusion drives the gain. This is the best next use of budget because it is a minimal, high-information extension of the leading configuration before adding more complex profile, aggregation, or encoder changes.

The strongest evidence so far is that single-profile multimodal PCA+ResNet with concat fusion outperforms RNA-only and image-only models, with weighted fusion only slightly worse. The key uncertainty is whether multiprofile representation plus aggregation can improve on this promising multimodal baseline. config_018 is the best next experiment because it makes the minimal logical extension: it keeps the best-supported encoders and concat fusion while testing multiprofile with a simple avgpool aggregation, helping isolate the effect of profile setting/aggregation before trying more complex transformer aggregation or other encoders.

The strongest evidence is config_018, where multimodal multiprofile PCA+ResNet with avgpool and concat reaches 0.619 accuracy and 0.610 F1, suggesting multiprofile aggregation is highly promising. However, only avgpool has been tested in this setting, leaving uncertainty about whether a more expressive aggregation could improve performance. config_020 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the same profile setting, encoders, and concat fusion, so it isolates the effect of aggregation. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the current best direction while testing an important unexplored design choice before moving to new encoders or other factors.

The strongest evidence so far is that multimodal multiprofile with avgpool and concat fusion is the best configuration (0.619 accuracy), clearly above the single-profile multimodal baseline and the transformer-aggregation variant. Fusion choice is still under-tested in this best setting: concat slightly beat weighted only in the weaker single-profile case. config_019 changes only fusion from concat to weighted while keeping the current best profile, encoders, and aggregation fixed, so it directly tests whether fusion method matters in the strongest known setting. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising direction, has high expected immediate performance, and isolates an important design decision without introducing multiple confounding changes.

The strongest evidence so far is config_019, which combines multimodal input, multiprofile, avgpool, and weighted fusion to reach the best validation accuracy and F1. The main remaining uncertainty is whether the current ResNet50 image representation is limiting performance, since image-only ResNet50 was weak while multimodal ResNet50 was strong. config_025 tests this by replacing only the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l while keeping the otherwise best-performing multimodal, multiprofile, avgpool, and weighted setup fixed. This is a clean single-variable comparison, potentially high-value if the image representation is a bottleneck, and avoids changing multiple design choices at once.

The strongest evidence is that multimodal multiprofile models with weighted fusion and avgpool aggregation outperform single-profile variants, with config_019 (PCA, ResNet50) best at 0.639 accuracy and 0.620 F1; config_025 shows ViT-L offers no clear gain, and avgpool already appears better than transformer for concat. The main untested design choice in this promising regime is RNA representation. config_031 changes only the RNA encoder from PCA to scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile, ResNet50, avgpool, and weighted fusion fixed, so it isolates whether a learned RNA representation improves over PCA. This is a high-value exploitation/exploration step under a limited budget because it extends the best-performing direction while reducing uncertainty about an important, currently sparse dimension.

The current best configuration is config_031 (scVI RNA, ResNet image, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion) with 0.678 accuracy and 0.646 F1, clearly improving over the same setting with PCA RNA in config_019. The remaining uncertainty in this strong lineage is whether a stronger image encoder helps when combined with scVI: under PCA, ResNet and ViT were very close (config_019 vs config_025), so the image-encoder effect is still unclear. config_037 changes only the image encoder from ResNet to imagenet_vit_l while keeping scVI, multiprofile, avgpool, and weighted fusion, isolating the image representation effect. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the best known setting, may yield a new best, and completes a clean RNA/image encoder comparison without changing multiple factors at once.
